title: An icon exported as SVG has no picture in it
goal: Draw an icon on a blank canvas and export it as SVG and the file is mostly a bitmap: the white background the canvas starts with is a picture layer, so it gets embedded whole, making a small icon a file of tens of kilobytes with a photograph in it. A flat colour is a rectangle, so write it as one, and let an icon leave as pure shapes.
notes: Evidence, from the walk that shipped with the SVG export task: Scripts/playtest/svg-export-walk.json writes /tmp/photonz-playtest/svg-export-walk/svg-export-3-icon.svg, and its log line reads 17270 bytes, every layer as shapes, of which about 17000 is the white background as base64 PNG. Two ways to tell a flat picture: ask the ImageStore for the bitmap and check every pixel is the same colour (cheap enough on export, and PixelField/BoxSweep already do this kind of scan), or catch it earlier where a blank canvas is made (BlankCanvas.swift) and give the document a flat background that is not a bitmap at all. The second is the better answer and the bigger change.
acceptance: A blank canvas background of one flat colour exports as a rect rather than as an embedded picture
An icon drawn on a blank canvas exports to a file with no base64 in it at all
A real photograph still exports as a picture, unchanged
Checked by rendering the written file back and comparing it to the app own render

log.note: TRIAGE 2026-09-14: moved up beside the pen tasks. The user asked for SVG export so icons drawn in the app can be handed over. Export landed, but an icon drawn on a blank canvas comes out as a file with a base64 bitmap of the white background inside it, which is the one thing that stops the file being handable. It is the last step of the ask rather than a polish item.
